_comment: Single source of truth for the Who's Who page (whos_who.html renders this at load). To grow the list, add an entry here — no HTML edit needed. 'section' groups the entry; 'order' sorts within a section. Descriptions are drawn from the tradition wikis (traditions/<key>/wiki.md Summary + Core claim) to avoid drift.

sections.title: The fifteen thinker-traditions
sections.note: These are the figures you can filter by in the Sociogram's checkbox cuts. Everything deeper refers to them by last name.

sections.title: Companion traditions & namesakes
sections.note: Not checkbox traditions, but the figures the system is read against and built around.

people.name: Levin
people.blurb: Biologist who argues cognition goes all the way down — bioelectric signaling steers morphogenesis, and even cells and tissues show goal-directed, basal intelligence.

people.name: Friston
people.blurb: Neuroscientist whose free-energy principle casts every living system as a model that resists disorder by continually minimizing prediction error.

people.name: Hoffman
people.blurb: Cognitive scientist who argues perception is a species-specific interface tuned for fitness, not a transparent window onto objective reality.

people.name: Hawkins
people.blurb: Neuroscientist and technologist whose Thousand Brains theory models the neocortex as thousands of parallel predictive maps of the world.

people.name: McGilchrist
people.blurb: Psychiatrist and literary scholar whose account of the divided brain reframes attention itself as the faculty that brings a world into being.

people.name: Fredrickson
people.blurb: Social psychologist whose research on positive emotion and positivity resonance grounds an empirical science of human flourishing.

people.name: Stump
people.blurb: Analytic philosopher who recovers Aquinas's metaphysics and account of knowledge — analytic Thomism — for contemporary debate.

people.name: Carroll
people.blurb: Theoretical physicist and self-described poetic naturalist working on cosmology, the foundations of quantum mechanics, and how meaning fits a physical world.

people.name: Arkani-Hamed
people.blurb: Theoretical physicist probing whether spacetime and quantum mechanics are emergent from a deeper, more austere geometric structure.

people.name: Wolfram
people.blurb: Scientist whose computational view of the universe seeks to build physics itself from simple rules running over evolving hypergraphs.

people.name: Kastrup
people.blurb: Philosopher and computer scientist defending analytic idealism: that consciousness, not matter, is what is fundamentally real.

people.name: MacIntyre
people.blurb: Moral philosopher whose tradition-constituted rationality and revival of virtue ethics supply the project's underlying method.

people.name: Rohr
people.blurb: Franciscan contemplative whose order-disorder-reorder pattern offers a complementary Catholic register for spiritual and intellectual growth.

people.name: Wright
people.blurb: New Testament historian and theologian whose five-act biblical drama models how a community improvises faithfully within a living tradition.

people.name: Loughran
people.blurb: Philosopher and physics educator at the University of Notre Dame, Tom built this C2A2 Wiki and Explorer on the model of accelerator/detector systems for high energy particle interactions.

people.name: Aquinas
people.blurb: The 13th-century theologian whose Summa Theologiae — its question-objection-respondeo engine for staging rival views — is the spine several programs are read against.

people.name: Habash
people.blurb: Host of the Summa in a Year podcast — the contemporary voice guiding the project's day-by-day reading up into competence in Aquinas's framework.

people.name: Karpathy
people.blurb: AI researcher whose proposal for agent-maintained wikis — a shared knowledge layer agents read from and improve — is the method this whole system is built around.
